t: A low-cost chip with dual-band Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth, Thread and Zigbee.
steps: Buy an ESP32-C5 board from a maker shop, such as the Seeed XIAO ESP32-C5 or the SparkFun Thing Plus.
Get a USB-C cable that carries data.
Install the free Arduino IDE on your computer.
Add the ESP32 board package in the board manager.
Pick your board and its USB port in the menus.
Upload the Blink example and watch the light.
Try the WiFiScan example to list nearby networks.
Fit a dual-band antenna on the XIAO before you test 5 GHz.
meta: Open Board. From $6.90. A few stores.
